La grève de la faim pour faire pression: Hunger Strike as a Pressure Tactic
Depuis maintenant plus d’un mois, certai: For more than a month now, some McGill University students have eaten nothing.
Des dizaines de gens, étudiants ou non,: Dozens of people, students and non-students alike, stage a die-in in front of the university in solidarity with the hunger strikers. Photo: Adrien Gaertner
Depuis maintenant plus d’un mois, certai: For more than a month now, some McGill University students have eaten nothing. It is their way of putting pressure on their school’s administration. Their demands are simple, one of the strikers tells us: “Divestment and disassociation from Zionist companies and universities.”
Nous sommes à la mi-mars. Malgré les que: It is mid-March. Despite the few warm days Montréal enjoyed over the past few weeks, it is rather cold today. That doesn’t stop the students from warming themselves in the sun outside on campus. This is where La Converse meets Chadi, one of the students carrying on an indefinite hunger strike. “It’s been 29 days now since I’ve eaten anything. I only drink water, electrolytes and broth,” begins the student, a cane in his hand.
Au début, Chadi menait sa grève de la fa: At first, Chadi was carrying out his hunger strike with Rania, another committed student. But last weekend, at the end of her 34<sup>th</sup> day of striking, Rania had to end her fast because of a hospitalization made necessary by severe dehydration.
En passant les portes emblématiques de l: Passing through the university’s iconic gates on Sherbrooke Street, no one can ignore the police cars parked at the entrance. “They’re always there,” Chadi confides. “Ever since we organized a few student sit-ins a few weeks ago, there’s often police here.”
« Dès que les attaques d’octobre sont su: “As soon as the October attacks happened near Gaza, I was extremely uncomfortable with how the university was handling it. Students were constantly getting emails from the administration about the tense situation on campus, but I found that the information being shared was very biased,” he says. In those emails, the administration asked students in particular to “remain respectful and demonstrate peacefully. [We] are in a university here, a place of learning and the advancement of knowledge. Our community has always been our strength.”
Au début de sa scolarité, Chadi, Montréa: At the start of his studies, Chadi, a Montrealer of Lebanese origin, befriended several students who share the same frustration he does. Caused by the university’s silence in the face of the violence perpetrated in Gaza, this frustration grew over the weeks, then the months. “We started sending emails to the administration, taking part in student walkouts, in demonstrations. We even organized picketing to block the entrance to the school,” the activist lists. “In the end, after seeing that it changed nothing, we got to a point where we had to find a more extreme way to get the university’s officials to finally listen to us.”
Le 28 mars à 13 h tapant, des dizaines d: On March 28 at 1 p.m. sharp, dozens of students gathered in front of the university’s Arts Building, right near Sherbrooke Street, and protested by staging a die-in in solidarity with people who, like Chadi, have stopped eating to get a reaction from university officials.
C’est comme cela que Chadi et d’autres é: That is how Chadi and other committed students organized to begin a hunger strike. Their request is simple: the institution must be held accountable, because it has not adopted the “policy against the genocide in Palestine” that was voted for by 78% of undergraduate students. The policy calls in particular for divestment from companies deemed complicit in genocide and in arms sales to the State of Israel, as well as for the severing of inter-university ties between McGill and organizations that are auxiliaries of the Jewish state’s policies, which are deemed repressive (Lockheed Martin and Safran).
« Une administration qui ignore ce qu’un: “An administration that ignores what a majority of its undergraduate students want, that’s pretty strange,” Chadi adds ironically.
Votée l’automne dernier, cette politique: Voted on last fall, this policy, titled “Policy Against the Genocide in Palestine,” was adopted at a general assembly of the Students’ Society of McGill University (SSMU). The Society demanded that the institution cut all ties with companies and institutions accused of being “complicit in settler colonialism, apartheid or ethnic cleansing against Palestinians.” Today, the policy is on hold, because the SSMU received a request for an interim and interlocutory injunction against it, filed by a student who believed it promoted antisemitism.
Chadi, étudiant au baccalauréat en psych: Chadi, an undergraduate student in psychology at McGill University. Photo: Melissa Haouari
En septembre dernier, Chadi a entamé un: Last September, Chadi began a bachelor’s degree in psychology. “I was really looking forward to starting my studies at McGill,” he admits enthusiastically. “I did all my schooling in French,” the Montrealer continues, “but I chose McGill because I wanted an exemplary education, the kind you get at one of the best universities.”
« Je ne savais pas combien cette école a: “I didn’t know how depressing this school would become for me.” This disappointment, he confides, comes from the fact that he did not expect the university he had chosen to be so steeped in a “colonial logic.”
Au moment d’écrire ces lignes, Chadi est: At the time of writing, Chadi is the only student continuing an indefinite hunger strike. He is aware that a statement like that can be confusing. That is why he takes the time to explain how he and the others carry out their activism.
« On a un système un peu particulier. On: “We have a bit of a special system. We have indefinite strikers – like me, for example –, rotating strikers and people who help with the other aspects,” he explains. “Some fast for a period of three or four days, then others take over. That’s their way of being in solidarity with the cause.”
Pour ce qui est de l’alimentation, les c: As for food, things are simple: “In our situation, we take water, broth and electrolytes. And by broth, I mean drinking the water from a pot in which we’ve boiled something. I call it a kind of ‘food tea,’” he says, laughing. “Tea and coffee are allowed, but anyway, that’s not nutritious,” he adds.
Le 15 mars dernier, une lettre ouverte r: On March 15, an open letter written by graduates of the university was addressed to the institution’s administrative and executive staff. This <l1>open letter</l1> has so far gathered more than 1,200 signatures from former students, professors and staff members, who are publicly showing their support for the hunger strikers and their demands. It lays out the university’s current ties with certain organizations and cites the cases of several universities around the world that have cut all relations with Israeli universities deemed “complicit in a genocide.”
Cette lettre rappelle également le rôle: The letter also recalls McGill’s role in history, the institution having been the <l1>first Canadian university to divest from holdings tied to the South African apartheid regime following the demands and pressure of the student body</l1>.
Ce qui frustre Chadi, c’est que malgré l: What frustrates Chadi is that despite the speed at which this movement is growing and the support it is attracting, it still remains almost invisible to those it wants to get a reaction from. The university administration has thus still not acceded to the strikers’ demands – nor to their request to hold a meeting under the conditions they want.
Après un échange de courriels entre les: After an exchange of emails between the activists and certain members of the administration, the situation remains at a standstill today, even as time runs out. Screenshots shared on the Instagram page of the McGill hunger strikers’ movement show that university officials did not keep their word to offer a space and a meeting with the main parties, under the conditions they requested. The screenshots show that a request for a public meeting between the students and the administration was made within a reasonable time frame in order to accommodate those who wished to take part. Later, the university proposed a closed-door meeting between the dean and the activists, to be held as soon as possible, out of “concern for the health and safety of the strikers,” a proposal the strikers refused because their request for a public meeting was not respected.
Il est à noter qu’au moment d’écrire ces: It should be noted that at the time of writing, the university has been silent and remains deaf to the strikers’ demands for 10 days.
« Pourquoi est-ce que l’administration s: “Why does the administration care about our health, but do nothing to respond to our demands?” he wonders. “I find that ridiculous.” Saying he feels betrayed, he hopes that the “hypocrisy” of those he points the finger at will not go unnoticed.
Nous tenons à préciser qu’au moment où n: We wish to clarify that at the time of publishing this article, no one within the administration has agreed to grant us an interview. Only one statement has been published: “We respect the right of students to pursue political goals and to express political convictions. Our priority remains the health and well-being of the students taking part in the hunger strike. [...] McGill has clearly stated that it will not cut its ties with Israeli universities and research institutions. We have reminded the students taking part in the hunger strike that there is a process for expressing their concerns about any of the university’s investments.”
